label: Glassflow
Colour
Colour source *Container colour is read from the tab itself, so tabs in different containers differ. Tabs with no container use the fallback below.*
Fallback colour *Used when a tab has no container, no folder, or the workspace has no colour set.*
Custom colour *Any CSS colour. Used when source or fallback is set to Custom.*
Darkness *Mixes the source toward black. 0% keeps Zen's pastel hue, 45% is a deep jewel tone.*
Second gradient colour *Used by gradients whose end is set to 'Fade to a second colour'.*
Glass

Colourless glass *On: blur only, no saturation or brightness shift, so glass never alters the hue behind it. Off: adds saturation and contrast, which looks richer but tints whatever is underneath. Turn this on if glass is introducing colour you did not pick.*
Glass intensity *Scales every sheen, rim and glow at once. 0 removes the glass look. The per-state switches decide where glass appears; this decides how strong.*
Sheen strength *The white highlight band only. Lower this if glass looks washed out rather than tinted. 0 removes the sheen but keeps rims and blur.*
Sheen direction *Which way the highlight band runs. Separate from each state's tint gradient.*

Stop flicker on window focus *Zen greys out inactive windows and light-dark() colours re-resolve when focus changes. With transitions armed that animates every time you click away and back. This disables transitions only while the window is inactive.*

Snap into place at startup *Sine loads this mod's stylesheet from JavaScript, after the window has already drawn itself with Zen's defaults. Button and font sizes therefore arrive a moment late, and because those properties are animated, the correction slides visibly instead of just being there. This holds transitions off until startup settles, so it snaps once. It cannot remove the delay itself, only the animation of it.*
Selected tab
Style selected tabs *Independent switch. Everything below applies only to this state.*
Tint strength *How much source colour this state starts with.*
Opacity *Fades the whole tab including label and favicon.*
Gradient direction *Independent of every other state.*
Gradient end *What the gradient fades toward. Transparent shows whatever is behind. Weaker tint keeps the same hue at the End tint value. Second colour blends toward the Second gradient colour.*
End tint *Absolute strength at the far end. Only used by the weaker-tint and second-colour modes.*
Gradient spread *Where the fade finishes, across the tab. 100% is edge to edge; lower ends early and leaves a flat run.*
Glass sheen *The white highlight band.*
Glass rim *A 1px inner highlight along the top edge.*
Outer glow *A soft tinted halo. Replaces the rim shadow, so it includes the rim when both are on.*
Frosted blur *One compositor pass per tab in this state. The most expensive option here.*
Blur strength *Only used when frosted blur is on for this state.*

Tabs, shared
Tab roundness *Corner radius. Arc rebinds Zen's --border-radius-medium; this overrides it for tabs only.*
Texture *An overlay pattern on every tab state. Plain CSS gradients, so the cost is one extra background layer.*
Accent bar on the selected tab *A 3px bar down the left edge. Replaces Arc's container glow, which uses the same layer.*
Hide Arc's container glow *Arc paints a blurred bar of container colour across the left half of every container tab. Usually the extra colour you see on the left.*
Tab strip
Gradient behind the whole strip *One wash spanning the full strip rather than per tab. Also gives frosted blur something with structure to work against.*
Strip strength *How strong the wash is at its start.*
Strip direction *Independent of every other section.*
Sidebar
Enable sidebar styling *Tints the sidebar background. Arc's compact sidebar opacity still applies underneath; set that first, then use this on top.*

Sidebar target *Which element gets the tint. Zen's layout differs between compact, collapsed and expanded, so if one target does nothing, try the next. Whole sidebar is the safest. Turn on the debug outlines to see which elements actually exist in your layout.*
Sidebar tint *How much workspace colour the sidebar carries.*

Fill strength *Scales the tint's own transparency. This is NOT element opacity: fading the element would fade your tabs and text with it, which is what the old Opacity setting did. 1 is full strength, 0.5 is half.*
Sidebar gradient direction *Independent of every other section.*
Glass sheen on the sidebar *Independent switch.*
Glass rim on the sidebar *Independent switch.*
Window buttons
Enable macOS-style traffic lights *Turn OFF Arc's own 'macOS style buttons' first.*
Position *Which end of the sidebar row the buttons sit on.*
Show colour at rest *Off: neutral grey until hovered.*
Vertical oval on hover *Only the button under the cursor stretches.*
Oval height on hover *A multiple of the diameter, applied on top of the Resting shape below. 1.3 with a resting height of 1.15 stretches further on hover; 1.0 cancels hover growth entirely.*

Resting width *Width as a multiple of the button's diameter, independent of height. 1.0 is normal width, 1.4 is noticeably wider, below 1.0 narrows it. Combine with Resting shape (height) for a capsule in either orientation.*

Resting shape *Height as a multiple of the width. 1.0 is a circle, 1.15 a subtle capsule, 1.4 clearly elongated. The corner curve stays fixed at half the button width, so taller values give flat sides with the same round caps rather than stretching into an ellipse.*

Width on hover *A multiple of the diameter, applied via a compositor transform so it cannot push the other buttons sideways. 1 means hover does not change width, matching Resting width means no change either. Try 1.3 for a button that widens rather than lengthens on hover.*
Show glyphs on hover *Triggered by hovering anywhere in the group, matching macOS.*
Glyph size *A fraction of the button's width. 0.62 is close to macOS. Renamed from the old percentage setting, because a stale percentage broke the sizing maths and made the marks vanish entirely.*
Button opacity *Fades buttons at rest. Hover restores full opacity.*
Glass sheen on buttons *Independent switch.*
Glass rim on buttons *Independent switch.*
Frosted blur on buttons *Cheap here: three small elements, not one per tab.*

Close colour *Proton purple-60, a jewel amethyst rather than a pastel. Any CSS colour works. Alpha near 0.78 keeps it readable as glass while staying saturated. Hover stacks a second pass to deepen it further.*
Minimise colour *Proton blue-60, a sapphire tone. Keep alpha around 0.75 to 0.85: lower washes out, higher stops reading as glass.*
Maximise colour *A deep emerald, replacing the pastel mint. Green is the one hue macOS already uses for zoom.*

When the window is not focused *Arc paints the stock red/yellow/green traffic lights on inactive windows, which is what was overriding your choices. All three options below restate your colours so Arc cannot leak through.*

On hover *Arc paints the stock red, yellow and green on plain hover. All three options restate your own colours so Arc cannot show through. Keep colour is the default: hovering no longer changes the hue at all.*
Hover intensity *1 means the colour does not change on hover at all, which is the default. Above 1 saturates further. This is separate from the hover fill below.*
Hover colour, close *Leave empty to deepen the resting colour instead. Set a colour here only if you want hover to shift hue rather than intensity.*
Hover colour, minimise *Leave empty to deepen the resting colour.*
Hover colour, maximise *Leave empty to deepen the resting colour.*
Diameter *macOS uses 12px, Arc uses 14px.*
Gap between buttons *macOS uses roughly 8px.*
Troubleshooting

Outline what Glassflow touches *Magenta on tabs, cyan on window buttons. For the sidebar: orange is the whole sidebar, gold is the compact background, pink is the titlebar. Whichever outlines actually appear are the elements that exist in your layout, so pick that one as the Sidebar target.*
Interface font
Set the interface font *Changes tab labels, menus and toolbar text. Never touches web pages. This box only changes the typeface. Font SIZE is a separate switch below.*

Font *Atkinson Hyperlegible Next is the current release and what the Braille Institute recommends: seven weights against the original's two, variable format, 150 languages, and a Mono cut. The extra weights matter here, because browser chrome uses several and the 2019 original forces the renderer to fake them. Entries marked for dyslexia follow the British Dyslexia Association style guide; the four marked 'ships with Windows' need no install. Free from Google Fonts, or brailleinstitute.org/freefont for Atkinson and opendyslexic.org for OpenDyslexic. An uninstalled font silently falls back to the system one.*

options.label: Comic Sans MS  -- dyslexia (ships with Windows)

label: Custom font family *Only used when Font is set to Custom. Type the family name exactly as installed, for example: Iosevka, Public Sans. Commas work as fallbacks. Not the same as Firefox Settings > Fonts, which only affects web page text.*
Letter spacing *Extra space between characters. The British Dyslexia Association recommends slightly increased tracking; 0.05em is a gentle lift, 0.12em is pronounced. Use 'normal' for none.*
Word spacing *Extra space between words. Roughly 0.16em is the usual accessibility suggestion. Use 'normal' for none.*
Line height *Mostly affects menus and multi-line labels rather than tab titles. 1.5 is the common accessibility recommendation. Use 'normal' for none.*
Interface font size

Set interface font sizes *Replaces the Customize Font Size mod: same four surfaces it covered (tab bar, workspace title, find bar, workspace icons), plus folders, the URL bar and menus. Turn OFF Customize Font Size if you enable this -- both target font-size on overlapping elements, and running both means whichever loads last quietly wins, whichever mod that turns out to be.*
Tab bar text size *Same element Customize Font Size calls 'Tabbar tabs'. Accepts em or px, for example 1.3em or 20px.*
Workspace title size *The current workspace's name, shown above the sidebar.*
Find bar text size *The in-page search bar, Ctrl+F.*

Workspace icon size *The workspace switcher icons at the bottom of the sidebar. CFS calls this an icon size but implements it as font-size, since the icons are glyphs; kept identical here for a clean replacement.*
Folder label size *Tab group names. Not covered by Customize Font Size.*
URL bar text size *Not covered by Customize Font Size.*
Menu text size *Right-click menus and dropdown panels. Not covered by Customize Font Size.*
Tab edges

Per-state edge strength *Unlocks separate rim strengths for selected, unselected, hovered and unloaded tabs. Each value is a multiplier on the existing look, so 1 is exactly what you have now and nothing changes until you move one. Glass intensity still scales all of them.*
Selected: top highlight *Multiplier. 1 is the current strength.*
Selected: edge ring *Multiplier for the faint ring around the whole tab.*
Unselected: top highlight
Unselected: edge ring
Hover: top highlight
Hover: edge ring
Unloaded: top highlight
Unloaded: edge ring

Custom edge geometry *Chooses which edge carries the light and how thick the ring is, rather than the fixed one-pixel top highlight. Separate from the strengths above so those stay usable on their own without changing the shape.*
Highlight offset across *Positive moves the lit edge right, negative left. 0 with a vertical offset gives the usual top highlight.*
Highlight offset down *Positive lights the top edge, negative the bottom.*
Edge ring thickness

Fade the edge light *An inset shadow rings a tab at even strength, which fights a gradient that fades. This redraws the rim as an overlay that fades along an axis, so the lit edge is bright where the tab's colour is and gone where it has faded. Takes over from the plain rim while it is on.*
Edge fade axis *Which way the edge light fades. Match tab gradient follows whatever direction the tabs already use.*
Edge fade reach *How far the light travels before fading out, as a percentage.*

Per-state edge geometry and fade *Unlocks separate offset, ring width and fade reach for each tab state, so a selected tab's edge can be lit and faded differently from an unloaded one. Any value left blank keeps the global setting above.*
Selected: highlight offset across
Selected: highlight offset down
Selected: ring thickness
Selected: fade reach *How far this state's edge light travels before fading out.*
Unselected: highlight offset across
Unselected: highlight offset down
Unselected: ring thickness
Unselected: fade reach *How far this state's edge light travels before fading out.*
Hover: highlight offset across
Hover: highlight offset down
Hover: ring thickness
Hover: fade reach *How far this state's edge light travels before fading out.*
Unloaded: highlight offset across
Unloaded: highlight offset down
Unloaded: ring thickness
Unloaded: fade reach *How far this state's edge light travels before fading out.*
